goal: Adds a standalone bitcoin-mine test program that talks to bitcoin-node over IPC to build and submit blocks
Gives developers a working example for building IPC clients against the Mining interface, e.g. Stratum v2 template providers
reviewability: Ready to review now, branch is current and CI is clean
One open architecture request (separate build flag so it isn't shipped by default) is unresolved but not blocking review
agreement: Sustained Concept and Tested ACKs across two years of rebases (Sjors, ismaelsadeeq, BrandonOdiwuor)
Nonblocking objection: binary shouldn't build/ship by default, author agrees but hasn't implemented it yet (sedited, fanquake)
Verified by testing IPC connection, tip retrieval, and block mining/submission (BrandonOdiwuor)
Naming and scope of the binary still debated without a final decision (sedited, ismaelsadeeq, Sjors)

categories.name: build
why: P4 because the CMake wiring is mechanical plumbing to add a new executable, not a build-system improvement
The one live build question, gating the binary behind its own flag so it isn't shipped in releases, is agreed but not yet done

categories.name: ipc
why: P2 because it is the only in-tree client exercising the libmultiprocess stack, since Python functional tests don't use it
Several later PRs and external forks already reuse plumbing introduced here, giving it real leverage

categories.name: mining
why: P3 because it gives cross-process coverage of createNewBlock, getBlock, and submitSolution that unit tests skip
Author himself concedes the original Stratum v2 motivation is now a bit stale, weakening the benefit

categories.name: tests
why: P4 because the added functional test mainly pins mining/IPC-specific behavior rather than general test infrastructure
Only generic contribution is a small addition to the test framework's Binaries class
